issue.description:
Direct testing against a real built pdftract binary (upstream pdftract repo, release build) shows that most of src/Pdftract/Client.php's methods are NOT just undocumented or duplicated-boilerplate (see bf-5g9) but are syntactically broken and cannot succeed at all, contradicting docs/plan/plan.md's framing that "the Client works by shelling out to a local pdftract binary."

Root cause: extract(), extractText(), extractMarkdown(), extractStream(), and getMetadata() all omit the required "extract" subcommand token that pdftract's clap CLI expects as the first argument (Commands::Extract in the upstream pdftract repo's crates/pdftract-cli/src/cli.rs). Confirmed by running the exact argv each method builds:

- extract(path) builds argv [path] -> error: unrecognized subcommand for the path itself
- extractText(path) builds argv [--text, path] -> error: unexpected argument --text found
- extractMarkdown(path) builds argv [--md, path] -> error: unexpected argument --md found
- extractStream(path) builds argv [path] -> same unrecognized-subcommand error as extract()
- getMetadata(path) builds argv [--metadata-only, path] -> error: unexpected argument --metadata-only found

Even after prepending "extract", two more bugs remain:
- extractText()/extractMarkdown() must pass an explicit output target after --text/--md (clap's --text/--md take a PATH value, e.g. a dash for stdout: extract --text <dash> <input>); passing the bare input path right after --text/--md causes clap to consume it as --text's value and then fail with "the following required arguments were not provided: INPUT" (reproduced).
- getMetadata()'s --metadata-only flag does not exist anywhere in the current pdftract CLI at all (confirmed: extract --metadata-only <file> fails with "unexpected argument --metadata-only found, tip: a similar argument exists: --md"), independent of subcommand placement. This SDK method cannot be fixed by argument-ordering alone; either upstream pdftract needs to restore/add a metadata-only mode, or getMetadata() needs reimplementing on top of a real flag (e.g. extract --json <dash-for-stdout>, filtered client-side for just the metadata block).

verifyReceipt(path, receipt) also has a semantic mismatch: it passes the receipt string as the bare second positional, which pdftract's VerifyReceiptCommand (upstream repo's crates/pdftract-cli/src/verify_receipt.rs) treats as a receipt file PATH, not inline content -- inline receipt strings require a separate --inline flag. Reproduced: passing an inline string produces "Error: Failed to read receipt from ..." because the CLI tried to read it as a path.

Only hash() is confirmed fully correct and working end-to-end (pdftract hash <file> returns a real fingerprint). classify() has correct CLI form (pdftract classify <file> parses fine) but the binary tested here was built without the "profiles" Cargo feature (pdftract's default feature set is empty in crates/pdftract-cli/Cargo.toml), so it errors at runtime needing that feature. search() similarly requires the non-default "grep" feature; the binary tested here doesn't have it, producing an unrecognized-subcommand error for grep -- verify against a feature-complete build before assuming search()'s argument construction is otherwise correct.

For comparison, the sibling pdftract-go SDK in the upstream monorepo (pdftract-go/pdftract.go) gets this right: its Extract-family methods all prepend the "extract" subcommand before --json/--text/--metadata-only etc. It also assumes the now-nonexistent --metadata-only flag, suggesting that flag was removed or renamed upstream after all SDKs were written and no SDK (php or go) has been updated since.

This bug affects the CURRENTLY COMMITTED, shipped src/Pdftract/Client.php on origin/main -- it is not part of the uncommitted ADR-1 HTTP-migration WIP (bf-4gq) and is independent of it (the same argument-construction bugs would need fixing in the HTTP request-building code too, if/when that lands, since the HTTP handlers wrap similar option semantics). It's also relevant to bf-5g9 (dedupe proc_open blocks) -- that bead currently says "keep behavior identical, this is a pure refactor," which would just relocate/preserve these bugs into a refactored shared method rather than fix them; the two should probably be done together, or this one done first.

Verify a fix by building pdftract with default (empty) features, matching a typical release build, then running each Client method against a small fixture PDF under tests/sdk-conformance/fixtures/ and confirming real output instead of a CLI parse error.
issue.title: Client extract/text/markdown/stream/metadata methods construct CLI args that fail against the real pdftract binary

issue.description: Once the ADR-1 HTTP-client migration (docs/plan/plan.md) is in place, add a Client::extractBatch(array $sources, array $options = []): array method that fires concurrent HTTP requests (e.g. via curl_multi) instead of forcing callers to loop and await one extract() at a time. This is the kind of batch PDF-processing workload the CLI-subprocess design could never support well (one OS process per call); it becomes cheap once the transport is HTTP. Depends on the HTTP client migration bead landing first -- do not start until Client has a working HTTP transport.

issue.description:
docs/plan/plan.md's ADR-1 (2026-07-20) decides: "pdftract-php will become an HTTP client against pdftract --serve, replacing the proc_open subprocess wrapper as the SDK's sole transport" -- covering all 9 documented Client methods (extract, extractText, extractMarkdown, extractStream, search, getMetadata, hash, classify, verifyReceipt).

Checked against the upstream pdftract repo's actual serve-mode implementation (crates/pdftract-cli/src/serve.rs): the HTTP server currently exposes exactly 5 routes -- root, POST /extract, POST /extract/text, POST /extract/stream, and GET /health. That covers only 3 of the 9 SDK methods (extract, extractText, extractStream). There is no HTTP route at all for:

- search() -- no equivalent of the CLI's grep subcommand
- getMetadata() -- no lightweight metadata-only endpoint (would have to reuse the full /extract response)
- hash() -- no equivalent of the CLI's hash subcommand
- classify() -- no equivalent of the CLI's classify subcommand
- verifyReceipt() -- no equivalent of the CLI's verify-receipt subcommand
- extractMarkdown() -- no dedicated route; markdown output is controlled by a markdown_anchors flag on /extract or /extract/text, not confirmed equivalent to the CLI's --md output

Additionally, no OpenAPI/schema description of the serve API exists anywhere in the upstream repo (no file matching *openapi* was found, and the serve module doesn't use an OpenAPI-generation crate), even though ADR-1's plan explicitly calls for regenerating/auditing the SDK's Models/Codegen tree "against the actual HTTP OpenAPI schema pdftract --serve exposes" -- that schema does not exist yet to regenerate against.

This means ADR-1's "sole transport" framing is currently unachievable for 6 of 9 methods without new upstream work in the pdftract repo itself (adding routes for search, hash, classify, verifyReceipt, getMetadata, and ideally publishing an OpenAPI schema for serve). bf-4gq (reconcile the WIP per ADR-1) does not currently call this out, and could otherwise proceed as if HTTP parity were just a client-side implementation task.

This needs a human decision, not just engineering follow-through, since it changes the shape of ADR-1 itself. Options to weigh: (a) coordinate/track the upstream serve-mode route additions as a prerequisite, (b) keep a CLI-subprocess fallback specifically for the methods HTTP can't reach yet (revisits ADR-1's rejected "support both transports" alternative, at least partially and temporarily), or (c) drop those methods from pdftract-php's v1 HTTP-only surface and re-add them once upstream catches up. Whoever picks this up should re-read ADR-1 in full and decide which of these (or another option) to adopt before bf-4gq's implementation proceeds past the 3 methods serve-mode already supports.
issue.title: OPS-GATED: ADR-1 assumes pdftract --serve covers all 9 SDK methods; only 3 have HTTP routes today

issue.description: The lab checkout has ~7 weeks of uncommitted, half-finished work (src/Client.php, src/Codegen/, src/Models/ at the src/ root, plus modified composer.json/README.md/phpunit.xml/tests/ConformanceTest.php) that starts migrating the SDK from a proc_open CLI-subprocess wrapper to an HTTP client, but only reimplements 2 of 25 model classes and leaves a stub Codegen/Methods.php ('This class will be populated with auto-generated methods'). docs/plan/plan.md ADR-1 (2026-07-20) decides the SDK should move to an HTTP client against 'pdftract --serve'. This bead is to execute that decision: finish the HTTP Client implementation, port the remaining model classes and the full exception hierarchy, delete the superseded src/Pdftract/ tree once nothing references it, and fix the composer.json PSR-4 autoload root consistently (src/ vs src/Pdftract/ -- currently the committed and uncommitted trees disagree). Read docs/plan/plan.md ADR-1 in full before starting.

issue.description: No proc_open() call in src/Pdftract/Client.php sets a timeout. A hung or pathologically slow pdftract invocation (e.g. a malformed/huge PDF) blocks the calling PHP process indefinitely, with no way for a caller to bound it. Add a constructor-configurable timeout (e.g. $timeoutSeconds, default a few seconds for metadata/hash, longer for extract/OCR) enforced via stream_select()/proc_terminate() on the child process. If ADR-1's HTTP migration (see docs/plan/plan.md) lands first, apply the equivalent as a curl CURLOPT_TIMEOUT / connect-timeout instead -- whichever transport is current when this is picked up.

Positive-half verification of the field-minimality pin (test_extract_forwards_options_as_the_only_snake_case_fields, tests/ClientBufferedRouteTest.php:331; fixtures FORWARDABLE_OPTIONS :187, FORWARDED_FIELDS :202) against serve.rs receive_pdf(). Per-field verdicts (forwarded):
- ocr_language => 'eng': real KNOWN_FIELDS member (serve.rs:805). Read raw, no parsing (serve.rs:869-873, params.ocr_language = Some(value)); consumed in build_options via parse_comma_list -> ["eng"], and the server default is also ["eng"] (serve.rs:978-982). camelCase ocrLanguage -> ocr_language unmangled (src/Client.php:260). Value round-trips verbatim; 'eng' is the documented default language code. CONCORDANT.
- pages => '1-3': real KNOWN_FIELDS member (serve.rs:808). Read raw (serve.rs:887-890, params.pages = Some(value)); carried into ExtractionOptions as pages and parsed by pdftract-core pages::parse_pages, which accepts the N-M 1-based shape ('1-3,7' is the docstring example, crates/pdftract-core/src/pages.rs:118). Value round-trips verbatim. CONCORDANT.
- full_render => 'true' (string): real KNOWN_FIELDS member (serve.rs:803). Read via parse_bool("full_render", &value).unwrap_or(false) (serve.rs:854-861); parse_bool accepts "true" case-insensitively (serve.rs:305), so the client's bool->'true' cast (src/Client.php:261) parses back to a real true. CONCORDANT.

Dropped entries (asserted absent by the same assertSame):
- noCache => false dropped is load-bearing and correct: the no_cache arm reads the field by PRESENCE only and never reads its value (serve.rs:850-853), so forwarding no_cache=false would set params.no_cache = true — silently disabling the cache. The exact-map pin catches any leak.
- ocrDpi => null dropped is correct: ocr_dpi is read only when present (serve.rs:874-878); absent -> ocr_dpi_override: None (server default).

(The pin is order-sensitive via assertSame, but the client deterministically produces this order and the server is order-agnostic — a stricter client-behavior pin, not a false server-contract claim.)

Observations, not defects in this pin: (1) the receive_pdf doc comment (serve.rs:777-787) omits `pages` although it is in KNOWN_FIELDS and parsed at serve.rs:887 — a Rust-side doc gap, outside this repo. issue.description:
Child 3 of 5. Umbrella: pdfphp-ee00f82b (mutation-proof the file-Source bytes pin). Kill leak position 2 of 5: the FILENAME leak. Depends on child 2 (pdfphp-e613f2b1).

Target: the multipart filename regressing from the fixed 'document.pdf' to the source path or a basename of it. Current code: src/Client.php:353 builds `new \CURLStringFile($pdf, 'document.pdf', 'application/pdf')` inside curlHandle(); $pdf there is already resolved bytes, so the mutation must thread the Source (or its path) through to curlHandle to make the filename echo it — e.g. pass the Source down and build the filename as `$pdf->getPath()` or `basename($pdf->getPath())`. Both variants are worth one run each if cheap; the basename variant is the realistic one because switching to `new \CURLFile($path)` basenames automatically.

The pin that must FIRE: assertDocumentUpload() in tests/ClientBufferedRouteTest.php (~line 1080), reached from BOTH test_a_file_source_uploads_the_file_bytes and test_a_file_source_with_options_sends_only_the_forwarded_fields_and_the_bytes — `self::assertSame('document.pdf', $upload['filename'], $request->describe())` (line ~1087) and `self::assertSame('document.pdf', $request->uploadedFilename(), $request->describe())` (line ~1092). These are source-blind by construction: any filename other than the literal 'document.pdf' fails regardless of what the temp file is named. Run at least the optionless pin; running both is better. Record test names, assertion output, exit codes.

Also CONFIRM (read-only, no mutation) that the remaining wire-identity dimensions are each pinned in assertDocumentUpload(): field name 'file' as the only uploads key (line ~1082), media type application/pdf (~1088), part size strlen(self::PDF_BYTES) (~1089), sha256 over the harness-captured part bytes (~1090), error 0 (~1091), plus uploadedContentSha256 in the optionless test. Note any dimension NOT pinned in your notes — that is a finding even if out of scope to fix here.

Steps:
1. Export PATH (see Acceptance). Run the pin(s) green first and record the passes.
2. Apply the filename mutation (path variant, then basename variant). Run the pin(s) after each. Record each: test name, full failure output, exit code.
3. Revert with `git checkout -- src/`. Verify `git status --porcelain -- src tests` is empty before finishing.
4. Record the evidence and the wire-identity confirmation on this bead's notes.

INERT-RUN TRAP (from prior rounds): a botched edit whose call site never threads the Source produces an inert run that looks like a pass. If the pin PASSES: first prove whether the mutation actually reached the wire (a leak that provably shipped with a green pin is a coverage gap; a leak that never shipped is an inert edit — fix the edit and re-run). Record any inert first draft honestly.

COVERAGE GAP: if the leak provably ships and no pin fails, strengthen the pin, prove it now FAILS on this mutation and PASSES when reverted, commit, and push to Forgejo origin. No force-push. Do not delete or weaken coverage belonging to any other slice; tests/Retired stays excluded and inert.

Acceptance:

Export `export PATH=/nix/store/22x54ar7f5sv6qpzbs635hbm9425gw83-php-with-extensions-8.2.28/bin:/nix/store/bfbww3vdbqmaz8p1jrknkxsjvv3zkv1h-composer-2.8.5/bin:$PATH` before any phpunit/composer call — vendor/bin/phpunit has a `#!/usr/bin/env php` shebang, so without it it exits 127 with NO output, which has been mistaken for a pass. - Each mutation is observed as a real failure of the intended pin, then reverted with git checkout; `git status --porcelain -- src tests` verified empty at close.
- Gotcha: `bead update --notes` REPLACES the entire notes field. Compose the full note in a /tmp file and write it in one call.

EXIT=0 — OK (2 tests, 23 assertions). Saved /tmp/pdfphp-3cfc87aa-baseline.txt.

Threading edit: curlHandle() signature changed from `string $pdf` to `Source|string $pdf`; both call sites (request() line ~382 and stream() line ~534) now pass `$pdf` instead of `$this->resolvePdf($pdf)`; inside curlHandle():
  $filename = $pdf instanceof Source ? ($pdf->getPath() ?? 'document.pdf') : 'document.pdf';
  $fields[self::FILE_FIELD] = new \CURLStringFile($this->resolvePdf($pdf), $filename, 'application/pdf');
Not inert: the Source provably reached the wire (failure output shows the mutated filename parsed off the multipart body).
EXIT=1 — 2 failures, both at tests/ClientBufferedRouteTest.php:1087 (reached from :385 and :435):
  1) test_a_file_source_uploads_the_file_bytes — Failed asserting that two strings are identical. --- Expected 'document.pdf' +++ Actual 'pdftract-buffered-92746779.pdf' (message prefix: POST /extract)

Note: curl put the FULL path in Content-Disposition, but the captured actual is the basename — the loopback harness is PHP, and PHP's multipart parser strips directory components from $_FILES['name']. Detection still fired because the harness temp file's basename differs from 'document.pdf'.

RUN 3 — MUTATION B: BASENAME VARIANT (the realistic one — `new \CURLFile($path)` basenames automatically)
Same threading; only the filename expression changed to:
  $filename = $pdf instanceof Source ? (basename($pdf->getPath() ?? 'document.pdf')) : 'document.pdf';
Not inert: same wire proof as Run 2.
EXIT=1 — 2 failures, both at tests/ClientBufferedRouteTest.php:1087:
  1) test_a_file_source_uploads_the_file_bytes — Actual 'pdftract-buffered-2583ce16.pdf'
  2) test_a_file_source_with_options_sends_only_the_forwarded_fields_and_the_bytes — Actual 'pdftract-buffered-d24bca72.pdf'
  Tests: 2, Assertions: 10, Failures: 2. Saved /tmp/pdfphp-3cfc87aa-basename-variant.txt.

RUN 4 — REVERT + RE-GREEN
git checkout -- src/ ; `git status --porcelain -- src tests` printed nothing (clean).
Pins again EXIT=0 — OK (2 tests, 23 assertions). Full suite EXIT=0 — OK, but some tests were skipped! Tests: 106, Assertions: 543, Skipped: 18 (skips are pre-existing environment skips, not failures). Saved /tmp/pdfphp-3cfc87aa-post-revert.txt and /tmp/pdfphp-3cfc87aa-full-suite.txt.
No inert first draft occurred: both mutations failed on their first run, with the mutated filename visible in the assertion diff.

WIRE-IDENTITY CONFIRMATION (read-only) — assertDocumentUpload(), tests/ClientBufferedRouteTest.php:1080-1093. Every dimension the task named is pinned:
- uploads key is exactly ['file'] — line 1082
- exactly one part in that field — line 1083
- filename === 'document.pdf' — line 1087 (the leak pin; fired in every mutant run)
- mime === 'application/pdf' — line 1088
- size === strlen(self::PDF_BYTES) — line 1089
- sha256 of the harness-captured part bytes === hash('sha256', self::PDF_BYTES) — line 1090
- upload error === 0 — line 1091
- uploadedFilename() === 'document.pdf' — line 1092
- uploadedContentSha256() pinned in the optionless test (test_a_file_source_uploads_the_file_bytes, lines 395-399) only, as expected — the options test relies on assertDocumentUpload.

DIMENSIONS NOT PINNED (findings, out of scope here):
1. The pin's two filename reads (1087 and 1092) read the same parsed $_FILES record — one wire dimension asserted twice, not independent coverage.
2. No test anywhere asserts the RAW wire filename (Content-Disposition text) or the raw body: RecordedRequest::rawBodyBytes()/rawBodySha256() exist but are never used in tests/*.php. Combined with the harness being PHP (whose parser strips directory components from the client filename), a full-path leak is only observable as its basename; if the temp fixture were ever named 'document.pdf', both filename mutants would become invisible to this pin. Mitigated today by the harness's random hex temp names, but a raw-body assertion would close it.
3. assertDocumentUpload() does not pin the request Content-Type as multipart/form-data for file-Source requests; that is pinned only on the bytes-source routes (tests/ClientBufferedRouteTest.php ~249 and ~276).

DISPOSITION: leak position 2 of 5 (filename) is killed — the pin fires on both realistic variants from both entry tests. No source or test changes were needed, so there is nothing to commit; verification-only bead. tests/Retired untouched and excluded. Working tree clean for src and tests at close.

Verdict: CONCORDANT — the file-Source pin is neither over- nor under-specified. No fix; no files changed, nothing committed (verification-only). Suite on PHP 8.2.28: OK (44 tests, 222 assertions), at baseline.

Dimension-by-dimension (tests/ClientBufferedRouteTest.php = "tests", src/Client.php = "client", serve.rs paths are /home/coding/pdftract/crates/pdftract-cli/src/serve.rs):

1. Field name — server-defined, tight. The server reads `field.name()` (serve.rs:816) and takes the document only from a part named `file` or `pdf` (serve.rs:819). Pinned by tests:972 `assertSame(['file'], array_keys($request->uploads()))`: exactly one upload, named `file` — the alternate `pdf` spelling, a rename, or a second upload all fail. Client: client:49 (`FILE_FIELD = 'file'`), client:308.

2. Filename `document.pdf` — NOT a server-read dimension: receive_pdf never calls `field.file_name()`; the only `file_name` in serve.rs is the server's own reqwest test module (serve.rs:1306). Pinned anyway as a source-invariance contract pin: tests:977 and tests:982, produced source-blind at client:308 (CURLStringFile with a fixed postname). It cannot spuriously fail for a file source — the postname does not depend on the path — and it is the pin that bars a `new \CURLFile($path)` regression, which would send `basename($path)` (the random temp fixture name) instead of the fixed name. Omission is also caught: a filename-less part is filed by PHP under $_POST, not $_FILES, so uploads go empty and tests:972 fails.

3. Media type `application/pdf` — NOT a server-read dimension: the server validates `%PDF-` magic bytes on the content (serve.rs:826-831) and touches the request-level Content-Type only through axum's Multipart extractor (serve.rs:534); the part's own Content-Type is never read. Pinned anyway as source-invariance: tests:978, produced source-blind at client:308 (explicit mime, not extension-derived). Catches omission — PHP would report `''`. Same verdict as filename: a deliberate contract pin with no misfire risk for either source.

4. Size — server-visible: the server reads the whole part body (serve.rs:820-823) and writes it to a temp file (serve.rs:836). Pinned by tests:979 `assertSame(strlen(self::PDF_BYTES), $upload['size'])`; the harness reports PHP's parsed size (tests/Support/loopback-router.php:96). Implied by the sha256 pin, retained for a distinct failure message; it describes the same bytes the server consumes, so it is not over-specified.

5. sha256 — THE server-read dimension (the bytes themselves are the extraction input and the magic-byte check). Pinned by tests:980 (helper) and restated with its own message at tests:392-396 inside the file test. The harness hashes the received content (`hash_file('sha256', $tmpName)`, loopback-router.php:92-94), so a match proves the file's bytes — not the path — arrived. Non-vacuous: tests:981 requires `error === UPLOAD_ERR_OK`, which is exactly the condition under which the harness hashes (loopback-router.php:92).

Why wire-identity holds structurally, not just assertion-by-assertion: the helper is shared — called by the bytes-backed happy paths (tests:251, 278), the options-bearing bytes test (tests:360), and both file tests (tests:382, 423) — so every dimension above is asserted identically for both source kinds against the same PDF_BYTES fixture. The client's encoding is source-blind by construction: `resolvePdf()` (client:236-239) reduces either source to a string before `curlHandle()` builds the body (client:308), so there is no per-source encoding branch that could drift.

Under-specification sweep — everything else the server reads on these routes:
- Method/path: pinned directly on the bytes-backed happy paths (tests:236-237, 268-269); for the file test it is enforced by the harness's loud unscripted-request 500 (loopback-router.php:209-219) — a file-source request to any other route/method fails before assertions run.
- Request Content-Type + non-empty boundary: axum's Multipart extractor (serve.rs:534) rejects non-multipart. The bytes-backed tests pin the header directly (tests:245-249, 272-276); the file test catches it transitively — a missing/mismatched boundary empties PHP's $_FILES, failing tests:972. No duplicate header assertion added: the header is produced by source-blind shared code and the transitive pin is airtight.
- Form fields: pinned to `[]` (tests:390) or the forwarded set (tests:422) against the fields the server actually reads (serve.rs:844-891, KNOWN_FIELDS serve.rs:798-809).
- Query string: pinned to `''` (tests:391); the server reads no query parameters on these routes — this is path-leak prevention from pdfphp-3a1ed8a2, already covered.
Nothing left unpinned that the server reads.

Over-specification sweep: nothing asserts a server-undefined behaviour that could legitimately vary. The two extra pins (filename, media type) are fixed client-contract values produced source-blind; boundary value, part order, header order, and Accept/Expect are left unpinned. The duplicated sha256 assertion (tests:392-396 vs tests:980) is redundant but intentional — distinct failure message and pdfphp-3a1ed8a2 provenance — and asserts a server-defined dimension, so it stays.

Coverage of other slices untouched; tests/Retired excluded and inert (phpunit.xml) — verified by the suite output above.

PIN 1 - forwarded-fields pin, test_extract_forwards_options_as_the_only_snake_case_fields (ClientBufferedRouteTest.php:331; consts :187/:202): correctly specified.

(a) Every FORWARDED_FIELDS name is a real, honored server field:
- 'ocr_language' => serve.rs:869-872 'params.ocr_language = Some(value)'; consumed in build_options via parse_comma_list -> ExtractionOptions.ocr_language.
- 'pages' => serve.rs:887-890 'params.pages = Some(value)'; 'ExtractionOptions { pages: params.pages.clone(), .. }'.
- 'full_render' => serve.rs:854-856 'parse_bool("full_render", &value).unwrap_or(false)'; 'full_render: params.full_render'.

(b) Every drop is load-bearing with the reason stated correctly:
- no_cache=false: serve.rs:850-853 '"no_cache" => { // Presence of the field means true (checkbox behavior) params.no_cache = true; }' - the value is never read, and it is genuinely consumed downstream (serve.rs:543 'let cache_disabled = params.no_cache || ...'), so a forwarded explicit 'false' string would silently disable the cache. The test comment states exactly this.
- ocr_dpi=null: serve.rs:874-877 'params.ocr_dpi = parse_int("ocr_dpi", &value).ok()' - an unparseable/empty value silently yields the server default. The comment attributes load-bearing only to no_cache and describes false/null generally as "server default", so it does not overclaim for ocr_dpi.
- timeout: takeTimeout() pops it before field building (src/Client.php:203-227); the server has no such name in KNOWN_FIELDS (serve.rs:798-809), so a forwarded timeout would only be warned-and-ignored (serve.rs:892-901) - detection is client-side, which the test acknowledges.

(c) bool-to-'true' serialization is the client's own deterministic choice, not over-specification: parse_bool accepts "true"|"1"|"yes"|"on" case-insensitively (serve.rs:303-311) and its result is consumed via unwrap_or(false), so any unrecognized spelling silently becomes false - the client must emit a canonical accepted spelling or the user's explicit fullRender silently no-ops. Which accepted spelling it emits is the client's wire contract (src/Client.php:261 "is_bool($value) ? 'true' : (string)$value").

(d) Whole-map assertSame minimality is justified: unknown fields are warned and ignored (serve.rs:892-901, "Unknown field - log warning and ignore (forward-compatibility)"), so a leaked field is invisible server-side and minimality is detectable only client-side; the test comment at :355-359 states exactly this.

PIN 2 - file-Source bytes pin, test_a_file_source_uploads_the_file_bytes (:364): correctly specified.
- Part name 'file' matches what the server reads: serve.rs:819 'if name == "file" || name == "pdf"'; client FILE_FIELD = 'file' (src/Client.php:49).
- Byte count and sha256 match the consumed surface: the server reads field.bytes(), requires real PDF magic bytes and >=5 bytes via validate_pdf_magic_bytes (serve.rs:333-352, "!data.starts_with(b\"%PDF-\")"), then writes those exact bytes to the temp file - so hash('sha256', fixture) + strlen is precisely what the server consumes, and it is what makes the path-as-content mutation detectable.
- Filename 'document.pdf' and media type 'application/pdf' are NOT read by the server (axum reads only the field name and bytes); they are the client's own deterministic CURLStringFile values (src/Client.php:308), so asserting them pins the client's wire shape - the same category as the 'true' spelling, not a server-behavior over-specification. The filename pin is additionally load-bearing: it is the "path must not travel as the filename" assertion (bead pdfphp-3a1ed8a2).
